documents.unit: University Policy 3710.2: Academic Integrity Standards and Process for Misconduct
documents.title: Academic Integrity Standards and Process for Misconduct (generative AI provisions)
documents.summary: The AI section (3710.2) of Wright State's academic integrity policy defines generative AI, bans its use in coursework unless the instructor states otherwise in the syllabus, lets instructors set their own protocols, and treats unauthorized use as an integrity violation judged by instructor expertise. The rest of the policy is the general misconduct process.
documents.stance_why: AI is banned by default: "If an AI statement is not included in the course syllabus and/or course content, then students may not use any type of generative AI", while instructors may allow use. A default ban unless explicitly permitted is restrict, not delegates, because the policy sets the fallback itself.

units.why: The sentence defines generative AI as "any type of software, i.e. algorithm, that is capable of creating, writing, or re-writing any form of content", which sets what the policy covers, so it is a definition (P61, informs, general).
units.anchor: any type of software, i.e. algorithm, that is capable of creating, writing, or re-writing

units.why: "Generative AI tools are distinct from search engines in that they generate content" draws the boundary of the policy by separating gen AI from search engines; this is scope-setting (P61), not a permission for search.
units.anchor: Generative AI tools are distinct from search engines in that they generate content.

units.why: "Submitting content created by any of the above means, either in its original or edited form, will constitute use of generative AI" extends the definition to edited AI output, fixing what counts as use; P61 fits as it defines scope, with a note that it also reaches edited output.
units.anchor: either in its original or edited form, will constitute use of generative AI.
units.fit_note: Also states that lightly edited AI output still counts as generative AI use, which is a scoping rule about submissions more than a definition of AI.

units.why: The passage says that for assignments built around "personal reflection, research, and the interpretation of content created by others" generative AI "may be undermined and will be graded accordingly". It gives a learning reason for limiting AI (P41), not a rule on its own; the grading consequence is stated only vaguely so P37 does not fit.
units.anchor: The use of generative AI of any kind in these assignments poses a risk
units.fit_note: Also says affected work "will be graded accordingly", an unspecified grading consequence.

units.why: "Instructors are free to establish their own additional protocols ... including allowing or disallowing some or all use" leaves the permission decision to each instructor, so P04 (instructor sets the rule), addressed to instructors before the course.
units.anchor: Instructors are free to establish their own additional protocols regarding student use of generative AI
units.frag_end: allowing or disallowing some or all use of such tools,

units.why: The proviso that protocols must be "consistent with applicable University policies, including those on academic standards and conduct" and attribution of others' intellectual property requires compliance with existing university policy, which is P77, not P04, since it limits rather than grants discretion.
units.anchor: Such protocols are consistent with applicable University policies, including those on academic standards and conduct

units.why: "Instructors who allow the use of generative AI in their classes incorporate protocols into their course syllabi and/or course content" requires a stated AI protocol, but only for instructors who allow AI; P09 fits with a note on that condition.
units.anchor: incorporate protocols into their course syllabi and/or course content
units.frag_end: how this technology may be used.
units.fit_note: The duty to state a protocol applies only to instructors who allow AI; instructors who disallow it need not say so, because the fallback ban applies.

units.why: "If an AI statement is not included in the course syllabus and/or course content, then students may not use any type of generative AI to complete coursework" is the fallback rule when a syllabus is silent (P06); it bans by default, so the stance is restrict.
units.anchor: then students may not use any type of generative AI to complete coursework.

units.why: "Using generative AI to complete any assignment or exam ... without express permission from the instructor, will constitute an academic integrity violation" classifies unauthorized AI use as misconduct, which is P36; exams are mentioned only inside this classification so P22 is not assigned.
units.anchor: without express permission from the instructor, will constitute an academic integrity violation
units.frag_start: Using generative AI to complete any

units.why: "Students who are unsure of policies or protocols regarding generative AI tools are encouraged to ask their instructor for clarification" tells students to ask when unsure, which is P10 with should.
units.anchor: are encouraged to ask their instructor for clarification.
units.frag_start: Students who are unsure of policies

units.why: "the instructor must carefully review the content for signs of such use" sets how suspected AI use is examined, but names no tool or evidence standard; nearest is P69 (what evidence to weigh), so P69 with a note.
units.anchor: the instructor must carefully review the content for signs of such use.
units.fit_note: Requires careful instructor review of the content but does not say what evidence suffices.

units.why: "The decision as to whether generative AI has been used by a student will be based on the instructor's subject matter expertise and discretion" makes instructor judgment the basis of an AI-misuse finding, an evidence standard (P69), not detector use (P40) or the formal hearing steps (P81).
units.anchor: based on the instructor’s subject matter expertise and discretion.

notes: Only wright-state-policy-3710 was included; the 2023 committee report was excluded in screening and not coded. Only section 3710.2 (AI) was coded; sections 3710.3-3710.6 are the general academic-integrity process (reporting, meetings, hearing panel, sanctions) and are not AI-specific, so they were skipped as boilerplate.
